extra.message: handoff(String envelope) Base64-decodes the attacker-controlled X-Dispatch-Envelope HTTP header (passed through unchanged from WebController.handoff -> DecisionClient.postWithHeader -> DecisionController.handoff) and feeds it directly into new ObjectInputStream(...).readObject(). Any authenticated staff user can submit arbitrary serialized Java objects, enabling gadget-chain remote code execution on the decision service.

extra.message: The /desk/relay/{passport} endpoint (permitAll in ChannelSecurity) calls com.nimbusds.jwt.SignedJWT.parse(passport) and immediately trusts the subject claim to build an authenticated SecurityContext, without ever calling verify()/checking a signature with a known key. Anyone can craft a JWT with an arbitrary 'sub' claim and an invalid/self-signed signature to log in as any user, including SUPPORT_ADMIN.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-287: Improper Authentication

extra.message: PartnerAssertionFilter reads the X-Partner-Assertion header and parses it with com.nimbusds.jwt.JWTParser.parse(assertion).getJWTClaimsSet() — this only parses the token, it never verifies a signature. The filter then builds an authenticated principal using the claimed 'sub' and the attacker-supplied 'desk_role' claim, letting any requester authenticate as an arbitrary existing user with an arbitrary elevated role (e.g. SUPPORT_ADMIN) via a forged, unsigned-equivalent JWT.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: renderEvidence() builds a single shell command string embedding the user-uploaded file's original filename ('original') and runs it via new ProcessBuilder("cmd","/c", "soffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir "+work+" "+staged).start(). Because the whole command is one string passed to cmd /c, shell metacharacters in the uploaded filename (e.g. '&', '|', '%VAR%') are interpreted by the shell, allowing arbitrary OS command injection.

extra.message: ticketReport(String domain) concatenates the admin-supplied 'domain' request parameter directly into a SQL string: "...where o.domain like '%"+domain+"%' ..." executed via jdbc.queryForList, with no parameter binding or escaping. A value such as "' OR '1'='1" or a UNION payload breaks out of the LIKE clause.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: directoryAgent(String uid) builds an LDAP search filter by string concatenation: ctx.search("ou=people,dc=acme,dc=test", "(uid="+uid+")", ctl) where uid comes straight from the @RequestParam on /api/directory/agents. An attacker can inject LDAP filter metacharacters (e.g. '*)(uid=*))(|(uid=*') to alter the search logic or exfiltrate unintended directory attributes.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query

extra.message: renderNotice(String template) passes the caller-supplied 'template' string directly as the Velocity template source to org.apache.velocity.app.Velocity.evaluate(ctx, writer, "caseNotice", source). Velocity templates can reach arbitrary Java classes/methods via its context and utility access, so an admin-submitted template (e.g. using $class.inspect(...) reflection tricks) can achieve remote code execution, not just text substitution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Server-Side Template Injection)

extra.message: renderAlert(String wording) compiles the caller-supplied 'wording' string as a FreeMarker template (new freemarker.template.Template("deskAlert", source, cfg)) and processes it. FreeMarker templates can invoke arbitrary classes via built-ins such as freemarker.template.utility.Execute or ?new, so this allows server-side template injection leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Server-Side Template Injection)

extra.message: previewRule(String expr) evaluates the raw, caller-supplied 'expr' string with ognl.Ognl.getValue(expr, variables). OGNL expression evaluation over untrusted input is a well-known RCE vector (the same class of bug behind multiple Struts CVEs), letting an admin-level caller execute arbitrary Java via OGNL static method/class access.

extra.message: writeTranscript(long id, String transcriptName) resolves the user-supplied 'transcriptName' directly against the transcripts directory (dir.resolve(name)) with no normalization or containment check, unlike upload()/download() in the same class which do normalize and verify startsWith(fileRoot). A value like '../../../../somewhere/evil.txt' lets any authenticated user (including CUSTOMER_USER, since this endpoint has no role restriction) write a file to an arbitrary path on disk.

extra.message: readTranscript(long id, String name) resolves the caller-supplied 'name' request parameter directly against the transcripts directory (dir.resolve(file)) with no normalization or startsWith(fileRoot) containment check, then opens and returns the file. A staff user can pass '../../../../etc/passwd' (or similar) via GET /api/tickets/{id}/transcript?name=... to read arbitrary files readable by the application process.

extra.message: profile(POST /profile) stores an arbitrary, attacker-chosen 'pictureUrl' string with no validation (line 62). picture() (GET /profile/picture) then server-side-fetches that stored URL via assets.get().uri(u.pictureUrl).retrieve().body(byte[].class) and returns the bytes to the caller. A user can set pictureUrl to an internal/metadata URL (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/...) and retrieve the response through this endpoint — classic stored SSRF.

extra.message: cover() sets a plain, unsigned cookie 'DESK_COVER' containing "<colleagueUsername>:<viewerRole>". coverUpdate() (POST /profile/{username}) later authorizes editing an arbitrary user's profile purely by reading that same cookie from the request and checking it ends with ':TEAM_LEAD' or ':SUPPORT_ADMIN' — with no server-side signature/HMAC on the cookie value. Since cookies are fully client-controlled, any user can set DESK_COVER=anyUsername:SUPPORT_ADMIN directly and update any other account's display name/picture without holding that role.

extra.message: The global CORS configuration allows any origin (allowedOriginPatterns("*")) together with allowCredentials(true) for all paths ("/**"), and addCorsMappings additionally does the same for /fragments/** and /tickets/**. This combination lets any external website make authenticated, credentialed cross-origin requests to the session-cookie-protected desk endpoints and read the responses, enabling session-riding data theft from any origin.

extra.message: importEncrypted() decrypts an attacker-influenced AES/CBC ciphertext and returns a distinct HTTP status for BadPaddingException (400) versus any other GeneralSecurityException (422). This observable discrepancy between padding failures and other decryption failures is the classic setup for a CBC padding-oracle attack, letting an attacker iteratively recover plaintext or forge ciphertext. The same pattern recurs in openCase() at line 62.

cwe: CWE-203: Observable Discrepancy
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: importEncrypted()/openCase() derive the AES key from env.getProperty("app.bundle-key", "local-bundle-key-change-me-32") — if the property is unset, a hardcoded, publicly-visible-in-source default key is used to decrypt customer-import bundles and case envelopes, and the CBC IV is taken directly from attacker-supplied ciphertext bytes with no integrity/MAC check, making the scheme both predictable and malleable.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: request() logs the raw, unhashed password-reset token with log.info("Recovery link queued for {} with key {}",user.email,token) immediately after generating it. extra.message: diagnostics("database"/"integrations") returns the live spring.datasource.password, app.scope-secret, and app.token-secret values verbatim in the HTTP response body. These are the HMAC signing secrets used to mint/verify every session and webhook token elsewhere in the system (SessionTokenFilter, ScopeTokenFilter, WebhookJob), so disclosure of this endpoint's output (e.g. via another vulnerability, log capture, or a compromised admin session) allows full authentication forgery across both services.

extra.message: browseEvidence() uses the uploaded part's client-supplied original filename unmodified as a subdirectory name: base.resolve(folder) with no normalization or startsWith(base) containment check, then lists that directory's contents. extra.message: credentialDigest() stores partner credentials as a single unsalted SHA-256 digest (HexFormat.of().formatHex(MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(...))) instead of a slow, salted password-hashing function (the same class already uses BCryptPasswordEncoder for normal account passwords in ChannelSecurity). This makes offline brute-force/rainbow-table attacks against a leaked auth_user.credential_hash column far cheaper than against the bcrypt-protected passwordHash column.
